points.name: Mushtifund Saunstha building
points.caption: One of Goa's oldest non-profit educational institutions, founded 1908, teaching in Konkani/Marathi rather than Portuguese. Source: @memorias_de_pangim (year is approximate — verify)
points.narration: This blue and white building has stood since 1930, home to one of Goa's oldest schools teaching in our mother tongue.

points.name: Bookworm Trust & Library
points.caption: Now Bookworm Trust & Library, House No. 127, Mala, Fontainhas — the children's library moved into this old blue-and-white building in September 2018

points.name: Mahatma Gandhi Road building (Virani Corporation)
points.caption: MG Road, Panjim — same building beside Virani Corporation, roughly 25 years before the current photo. Source: @memorias_de_pangim (year is approximate — verify)

points.name: U.S. Polo Assn., MG Road
points.caption: Now a U.S. Polo Assn. store, Survey No. 1625, MG Road, Panaji — beside Virani Corporation

points.name: Calangute Beach entrance
points.caption: Calangute Beach's old circular entrance plaza and steps down to the sand. Source: @retrogoa (posted 2020, photo dated 1992)

points.name: Calangute Beach
points.caption: Calangute Beach today — shacks, sunbeds and boats now line the same stretch of sand (exact photo year approximate)

points.name: Tito's Lane
points.caption: Tito's Lane, Baga, long before it became Goa's best-known nightlife strip — a quiet unpaved lane lined with palms. Source: @vintagegoa.memories (year is a rough guess — no date given, verify)

points.name: Tito's Lane
points.caption: Tito's Lane today at 2am — bars, spas, tattoo shops and crowds line the same stretch

points.name: Mandovi River billboard hillside
points.caption: The Reis Magos/Betim hillside across the Mandovi from Panjim — Kingfisher's sign has anchored this view for decades, though the surrounding ads (Spartan Beer, Sanjay Ghodawat Group) have changed. Year approximate, per your note (~1980s-90s) — verify

points.name: Mandovi River billboard hillside
points.caption: Same hillside today — Kingfisher still there, now alongside Casino Pride, Bellagio, LIC and Shikhar signage

points.name: Panaji Church (Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception)
points.caption: Panjim's iconic church and grand staircase. Year approximate, per your note (~1980s-90s) — this source photo has a stylized filter applied, so treat the exact date as unconfirmed until verified
points.narration: Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception Church has watched over Panjim since 1619, its grand staircase welcoming pilgrims for centuries.

points.name: Panaji Church (Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception)
points.caption: The same church and staircase today, largely unchanged in form since it was completed in 1619 and rebuilt in Baroque style over the centuries

points.name: Adil Shah Palace
points.caption: Also known as Idalcão Palace or the Old Secretariat — built c.1500 as a summer palace for Yusuf Adil Shah of Bijapur, later the Portuguese governors' residence. Year approximate — verify against your source.
points.narration: This palace was built around 1500 as a summer retreat for the Sultan of Bijapur, before becoming home to Portuguese governors.

points.name: Adil Shah Palace
points.caption: Today home to the Goa State Museum, still standing on the Mandovi riverfront — the oldest surviving colonial-era building in Panjim.

points.name: São Tomé
points.caption: São Tomé, one of Panjim's oldest wards, facing the riverfront just north of Fontainhas — named after the Portuguese word for 'little fountain.' YEAR PLACEHOLDER — replace with your source's actual date.
points.narration: São Tomé means 'little fountain' in Portuguese, named for the natural springs that once watered this riverside quarter.

points.name: São Tomé
points.caption: São Tomé today — still one of the quieter heritage quarters bordering Fontainhas, with its mix of Hindu and Portuguese-era houses.

points.name: Tobacco Square
points.caption: Largo dos Tabaqueiros (Tobacco Square), named for the tobacco trade once conducted here — later home to a customs post and the Goa Mint. YEAR PLACEHOLDER — replace with your source's actual date.
points.narration: Tobacco Square was once the heart of Panjim's commerce, where tobacco traders and customs officials shaped the city's economy.

points.name: Tobacco Square
points.caption: Today the square houses the General Post Office and the São Tomé Chapel, at the edge of the Fontainhas heritage walk.

points.name: Azad Maidan
points.caption: Originally Largo Afonso de Albuquerque (Praça de Sete Janelas), built 1843 with a domed monument to the Portuguese general. YEAR PLACEHOLDER — replace with your source's actual date.

points.name: Azad Maidan
points.caption: Renamed Azad Maidan ('Freedom Ground') after Goa's liberation — now home to the Martyrs' Memorial honoring Tristão de Bragança Cunha and 67 named freedom fighters.

points.name: Casa Dempo
points.caption: Casa Dempo on MG Road (then Afonso de Albuquerque Road), a traditional Hindu heritage house established around 1810. Photo reportedly c.1880, per Central Library archives — verify against your own source.
points.narration: Casa Dempo has stood on this road since 1810, a grand Hindu heritage house representing Goa's architectural diversity.

points.name: Casa Dempo
points.caption: Casa Dempo still stands on MG Road today, near the old Government Printing Press building.

points.name: Patto Bridge
points.caption: Patto Bridge over Ourem Creek — the Panjim-side extension of the Ponte de Linhares causeway, built by Jesuits around 1632-34. YEAR PLACEHOLDER — replace with your source's actual date.

points.name: Patto Bridge
points.caption: Patto Bridge today, connecting Fontainhas to the Patto business district, flanked by newer traffic and pedestrian bridges alongside it.

points.name: Panaji Church (Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception)
points.caption: An earlier view of Panjim's iconic church, completed in 1619 and rebuilt in Baroque style over the centuries. YEAR PLACEHOLDER — replace with your source's actual date.
